newsitem.title: USA: Russia finmin sees debt rating in next 10 days.
newsitem.headline: Russia finmin sees debt rating in next 10 days.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Tuesday that Russia's country debt rating, seen as a vital prerequisite for its planned debut Eurobond issue, should be known in the next days.
Livshits, arriving for the plenary session of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, told reporters: "There is not long left to wait."
"The latest will be in the next 10 days," he added.
Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on Tuesday and traders cited rumours European rating agency IBCA could assign Russia a BB plus rating this week.

Russian officials have said Russia will make a first issue of $300-500 million of Eurobonds this year. It has mandated JP Morgan and SBC Warburg to manage the issue and officials have said the first bonds could be issued later this year.
Asked if the volume to be issued had been decided, Livshits said, "We have plans in this regard but one cannot speak prematurely. ... Soon all will be known."
